sentences.text: A private complaint under Section 200 of Cr.PC was filed by the 1st respondent for the offences under Sections 406, 418, 420, 120B, 149 of IPC, alleging that, two complaints were filed by the 1st respondent against the members of the Society and in the proceedings, the petitioners conniving with each other entered into a compromise and filed a petition under Section 320(2) of Cr.PC for compounding of the offences by filing a false affidavit.
The learned Magistrate on the basis of the false affidavits compounded the offences.
The learned Magistrate referred the complaint to the police for investigation under Section 156(3) of Cr.PC.
The registration of FIR is impugned in this petition.

2. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners submits that, the offences against the petitioners are cognizable and the complaint filed without complying with Section 154(1) and (3) of Cr.PC is not maintainable as held by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Priyanka Srivastava Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287.

entities.text: Priyanka Srivastava Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Others reported in (2015) 6 SCC 287
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submit that the compounding of offences against the member of the Society was set aside by the learned Sessions Judge in a criminal revision petition and as such, the registration of FIR is impermissible.

3. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.1 submits that, the petitioners - accused on the basis of false affidavits filed a petition under Section 320(2) of Cr.PC for compounding of the offences without the knowledge of the respondent No.1.
Hence, the allegation made in the complaint disclose the commission of the aforesaid offences and as such, the registration of FIR does not warrant any interference.
4. I have examined the submissions of the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
5. The offences alleged against the petitioners are cognizable.

The complainant was required to approach the jurisdictional police before lodging the private complaint to register the FIR, and upon refusal to register the FIR, the respondent No.1 was required to approach the higher officer for taking action against the petitioners - accused.
In the instant case, the 1st respondent without complying with Section 154(1) and (3) of Cr.PC has filed the private complaint.

In view of the ration enunciated by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Priyanka Srivastava (supra), the complaint C S S Kashyap vs S Shivanna on 21 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160178714/
5 filed by the respondent No.1 without complying with the mandatory provision contained in Sections 154(1) and (3) of Cr.PC is not maintainable.

sentences.text: Hence, the continuation of criminal proceedings will be an abuse of process of law.

Accordingly, I pass the following:
ORDER i) Criminal petition is allowed.
ii) The impugned proceedings in PCR No.1/2017 pending on the file of the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Mysuru, insofar as the petitioners - accused No.1 to 15 is hereby quashed.
iii) Liberty is reserved with the 1st respondent to approach the jurisdictional Court in which the false affidavits were alleged to have been filed by the petitioners - accused for taking appropriate action in accordance with law.
